channel.title: Worth Guides
channel.description: Practical personal finance guides from Worth.

item.title: The 10/10/10 Rule for Better Spending Decisions
item.description: How the 10/10/10 decision rule stops impulse buys: ask how you'll feel in 10 minutes, 10 months and 10 years — with worked examples.

item.title: The 30-Day List: Kill Impulse Buys Before They Happen
item.description: How the 30-day list works: write it down, wait 30 days, buy only what you still want. A simple system that ends most impulse spending.

item.title: The 50/30/20 Rule Explained, With a Simple Worksheet
item.description: How the 50/30/20 budget splits your take-home pay into needs, wants and savings — with examples, mistakes and when to adjust the ratios.

item.title: The 52-Week Money Challenge (Easier Variations)
item.description: How the 52-week savings challenge works, why the standard version fails in December, and three easier versions that still build the habit.

item.title: Add Friction to Spending: Spend Less Without Willpower
item.description: How adding friction — saved cards, app deletions, cooling-off queues — cuts spending automatically, based on how behavior actually works.

item.title: Automate Your Finances: Set It and Forget It
item.description: How to automate salary routing, bills, savings and investments so the right money moves before you can spend it — a full setup guide.

item.title: Brand vs Generic: Where Switching Actually Saves Money
item.description: A practical look at brand-name versus generic products — which swaps save real money, which keep quality, and where store brands win outright.

item.title: How to Make a Budget You'll Actually Stick To
item.description: A realistic budgeting system for people who quit budgets: fewer categories, a fun line item, and a review rhythm that survives real life.

item.title: Buyer's Remorse: How to Avoid It and Recover Fast
item.description: Why buyer's remorse happens, the pre-purchase checks that prevent it, and what to do in the 30 days after a regretted buy.

item.title: Cash Stuffing: How the Envelope Method Works Today
item.description: What cash stuffing is, how to set it up with envelopes or a binder, and the pros and cons compared with digital budgeting.

item.title: Your Daily Coffee Habit Costs More Than You Think
item.description: The real annual and 10-year cost of a daily coffee run, with the math, break-even against brewing at home, and a guilt-free middle path.

item.title: Turn Any Price Into Hours of Your Life
item.description: The cost-of-time method: converting purchase prices into hours of work to judge whether something is truly worth buying.

item.title: The Real Cost of Eating Out (Formula + Examples)
item.description: How much takeout and restaurant meals really cost per year — the math, the hidden add-ons, and a middle path that keeps dinners out enjoyable.

item.title: The Envelope Budgeting System, Explained (Cash or Digital)
item.description: How envelope budgeting works, which expenses belong in envelopes, and how to run the system with cash, cards or a budgeting app.

item.title: 27 Frugal Habits That Don't Feel Like Deprivation
item.description: Practical frugal living habits for food, home, shopping and energy — the ones that save real money without making life smaller.

item.title: Unit Pricing: The Grocery Hack Most Shoppers Skip
item.description: What unit pricing means at the supermarket, how to read price-per-unit labels, and where bigger packs silently cost more.

item.title: Gym Membership Break-Even: When It's Actually Worth It
item.description: How to calculate gym membership cost per visit, the break-even point versus home workouts, and how to cancel or pause without overpaying.

item.title: Impulse Buying: Why It Happens and How to Stop
item.description: The psychology behind impulse purchases — triggers, dopamine and friction — plus practical rules that stop unplanned spending.

item.title: The Latte Factor: Rethinking Small Splurges
item.description: What the latte factor means, the real math behind daily small purchases, and how to apply it without becoming joyless about money.

item.title: Lifestyle Creep: The Silent Savings Killer
item.description: What lifestyle creep is, why raises vanish, and how to keep income growth from being swallowed by new spending habits.
